title: French National Quantum Strategy Backs €14M ($16M USD) Qubit Control 2030 Consortium to Scale Cryogenic Photonic Interconnects - Quantum Computing Report
gist: France 2030 is funding the €14M, 48-month Qubit Control 2030 (QC2030) consortium led by VIQTHOR with Isentroniq, Silent Waves, Radiall and SEDI-ATI Fibres Optiques to build a sovereign photonic/superconducting control and readout chain replacing copper coax, targeting 1,000-qubit (2028) and 10,000-qubit (2030) single-cryostat demonstrators. Control electronics and cabling are said to be over 70% of quantum hardware cost (~€60,000/qubit).

insights.claim: Control electronics and coaxial cables account for more than 70% of total quantum computer hardware costs, roughly €60,000 per qubit, and create severe thermal-load and space constraints inside dilution refrigerators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The control/interconnect stack, not qubits, is where most hardware cost sits; vendors that cut it capture outsized value.

insights.claim: QC2030 aims to combine photonic modulation, signal multiplexing and superconducting flex interconnects to eliminate the wiring bottleneck limiting single-cryostat qubit counts for superconducting and spin qubit platforms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Photonic control links are a key enabler for 10,000-qubit-class machines.

insights.claim: QC2030's Isentroniq targets replacing 40,000 copper cables at 10,000 qubits with 32 optical cords, while Silent Waves targets a 1,000x reduction in cryogenic footprint and heat dissipation via quantum-limited TWPAs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Aggressive targets that, if met, would sharply lower cryogenic system cost per qubit.

insights.claim: VIQTHOR's photonic-electronic control chips in QC2030 aim to cut per-qubit control cost 10x by 2030 and 100x by 2040.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A concrete cost-curve target to benchmark VIQTHOR and competing control-stack vendors.

insights.claim: The French National Quantum Strategy is providing €14 million ($16 million) of France 2030 funding, operated via Bpifrance's i-Démo program and labeled by Systematic Paris-Region, for the 48-month QC2030 consortium led by startup VIQTHOR.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Public money is flowing to enabling-technology startups, not just qubit makers.
insights.locator: The French National Quantum Strategy has announced

insights.claim: QC2030 unites five French enabling-technology companies: VIQTHOR, Isentroniq, Silent Waves, Radiall and SEDI-ATI Fibres Optiques, covering control chips, flex cabling, TWPA amplifiers, cryogenic RF interconnects and optical fiber feedthroughs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Radiall is an established connector maker gaining quantum exposure; the others are smaller private players.

insights.claim: From October 2026 to September 2030, QC2030 teams will co-locate at the iXcampus hub in Saint-Germain-en-Laye to validate single-cryostat demonstrators of 1,000 controlled qubits in 2028 and 10,000 qubits in 2030.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Milestones to track: 2028 1,000-qubit and 2030 10,000-qubit cryostat demos.

insights.claim: French National Quantum Strategy coordinator Loïc Le Loarer said securing domestic supply across cryogenic interconnects, amplifiers and photonic links is essential to industrializing fault-tolerant quantum computers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum supply chains are being treated as sovereign/strategic, implying continued state support and possible protectionism in Europe.

insights.claim: QC2030 is designed to complement France's PROQCIMA quantum processor development program by supplying the control and readout chain.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: France is funding a full vertical stack, with QC2030 as the enabling layer for PROQCIMA processors.
